steps.label: T1 — relaxation
steps.sub: How long |1⟩ takes, on average, to decay back down to |0⟩

steps.label: T2 — dephasing
steps.sub: How long a superposition keeps its precise phase before noise scrambles it

steps.label: Different physics
steps.sub: A qubit can lose phase information without losing any energy at all

steps.label: Both measured directly
steps.sub: T1 via a relaxation experiment, T2 via Ramsey or spin-echo

caption: T2 can never exceed 2×T1 — it equals that ceiling only when pure dephasing (Tφ) is negligible. Real devices almost always sit below it.

steps.label: Every gate takes time
steps.sub: And every qubit decays and dephases the whole time, busy or idle

steps.label: Run time vs. T1/T2
steps.sub: A significant fraction of either, and the final measurement turns to noise

steps.label: The trend
steps.sub: Early devices: nanoseconds-to-microseconds. Recent devices: tens to a few hundred microseconds
